text: Good morning, Pip! Race you to the water!
Ollie, the water is gone!
It was right here yesterday!
Why does the water go away?
Let's find out!
Maybe the sea is hiding.
Maybe it went on a trip!
Even the snails are leaving.
I know! The sea ran away. Easy!
Why would the sea run away?
Maybe it got bored. Or hungry!
I don't think seas get hungry.
The sand is shaped like waves. So the water was here!
I'll go find it. Follow me!
Ollie, wait! Bean is still back there!
Oops. Sorry, Bean. Let's go together.
Ha! I've got a faster way!
Gus, your faster ways always go wrong.
Not this time! We bring the sea back ourselves!
How, Gus?
Buckets! Lots and lots of buckets!
What if we try it the careful way?
Let's watch Gus try first. Then we ask Gran Mari.
See? One bucket, one big splash!
Hey! Where did it go?
Whoa, whoa, whoaaa!
Are you okay, Gus?
I'm fine! I did that on purpose!
Did you slip, Gus?
No! I was testing the water. It's wet. Very wet.
Your bucket water sank into the sand.
It was already wet, so it doesn't count!
Maybe buckets can't bring the sea back.
We need help. Let's ask Gran Mari.
Well now, a soggy seagull and a worried otter. What's all this?
Gran Mari, why does the water go away?
Oh, that is a good question, Ollie. Let's find out together.
This bowl is a pretend ocean. Watch the water, and watch slowly.
It moves! High on one side, low on the other!
See the moon? It pulls on the sea, just a little. Like a very gentle tug.
So the moon makes the water go up and down?
Yes. The water rises up the beach. Then it slides back out. Two times every day.
The water didn't run away! It's just out for a while!
So how long until it comes back?
Well now, what do you think happens next?
It slides back to the beach!
The sea keeps its own clock. We can't hurry it. But we can watch it.
Try it at home! Put water in a bowl. Tilt it very slowly. Watch the water climb one side. Watch it slide away from the other.
This is our water line. We wait and we watch.
I can't wait anymore! I'll go get the sea myself!
Wait!
Okay, okay. I fibbed before. My bucket water didn't count. It all sank away.
I'm sorry I said it was already wet.
Thanks for telling us the truth, Gus.
It came back all by itself!
Gran Mari was right! We waited and watched!
Time for my Wonder Pocket! Three things we learned.
One. The moon gently pulls on the sea.
Two. The water goes up and down two times a day.
Three. The sea always comes back. We just have to wait.
And one kind thing to try today. Wait for a friend.
Bye, everybody! Next time, I'll wait too!
